title: The Pot of Gold
summary: A peasant finds buried gold on land he just bought and insists on returning it to the seller. Birbal resolves the noble dispute.
full_text:
A poor but honest farmer named Madhav saved money for ten years to buy a fallow field from his neighbor, Keshav. A week after the sale, while plowing the rocky soil, Madhav's plow struck a heavy earthen pot. Digging it up, he found it filled with five hundred ancient gold coins!

Instead of keeping the fortune, Madhav carried the pot straight to Keshav's house: 'Brother Keshav, take this pot. I bought only the surface soil to grow wheat; I did not purchase this buried treasure. It belongs to you!'

Keshav refused to touch it: 'No, Madhav! I sold you the entire field, from the surface down to the center of the earth. Whatever lies within that soil is yours by right!'

Neither man would take the gold, arguing over who had the right to be honest! Unable to agree, they brought the pot before Emperor Akbar.

Akbar was amazed: 'In my court, men fight tooth and nail to steal from one another! Here are two men fighting because neither wishes to take gold!'

Akbar asked Birbal to resolve the dispute.

Birbal questioned both men: 'Madhav, do you have children?'

'Yes, my lord, an honest son who helps me farm.'

'And Keshav, do you have children?'

'Yes, wise minister, a virtuous daughter of marriageable age.'

Birbal smiled broadly: 'The solution is blessed by heaven! Let Madhav's son marry Keshav's daughter! Use the gold coins to buy them a fine home, farm tools, and livestock as their wedding gift. In this way, the treasure will remain within both families without staining the conscience of either father!'

The courtiers cheered with delight, and both farmers embraced with tears of joy. Akbar praised Birbal for turning a legal paradox into a celebration of virtue and family unity.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Pot of Gold"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
